title: A ring map is smooth iff the morphism of spectra is smooth
statement: Let $\varphi:R\to S$ be a homomorphism of commutative rings and $\operatorname{Spec}\varphi:\operatorname{Spec}S\to\operatorname{Spec}R$ the induced morphism of affine schemes [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Then $\operatorname{Spec}\varphi$ is smooth in the sense of [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms] (locally of finite presentation and formally smooth) if and only if the ring map $\varphi$ is smooth in the sense of [def-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map] ($S$ finitely presented over $R$, $H_1(L_{S/R})=0$, $\Omega_{S/R}$ finite projective).

source.place: Morphisms, Lemma Tag 01V6 (lemma-smooth-characterize, line 7048), (1)<=>(2) with U = Spec S, V = Spec R, for the smooth morphisms of Section Tag 01V4 (Definition Tag 01V5, affine-locally by smooth ring maps, Algebra Definition Tag 00T2); for the notion of [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms] (locally of finite presentation and formally smooth, Definition Tag 02H0) the statement is the affine case of More on Morphisms, Lemma Tag 02H6 (lemma-smooth-formally-smooth, literature/stacks-project/more-morphisms.tex line 3190), with Lemma Tag 02H4 (lemma-affine-formally-smooth) and Algebra, Proposition Tag 00TN (proposition-smooth-formally-smooth, algebra.tex line 38169)

proof.text: *Notation.* Write $f=\operatorname{Spec}\varphi:X=\operatorname{Spec}S\to Y=\operatorname{Spec}R$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Since $\mathcal O_X(X)=S$, $\mathcal O_Y(Y)=R$ and $f$ is $\operatorname{Spec}$ of $\varphi$, the ring map $\mathcal O_Y(Y)\to\mathcal O_X(X)$ induced by $f$ on the affine opens $X$ and $Y$ (with $f(X)\subseteq Y$) is $\varphi$.

source.place: Schemes, Lemma Tag 01I2 (schemes-lemma-category-affine-schemes): Spec is an equivalence between rings and affine schemes, with Gamma(Spec A, O) = A

proof.text: *($\Rightarrow$) finite presentation.* Assume $f$ is smooth in the sense of [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms], so $f$ is locally of finite presentation [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation] and formally smooth [def-sbc-formally-smooth]. By [lem-weil-pbc-lfp-affine-opens-finite-presentation] applied to the affine opens $U=X$ and $V=Y$, the ring map $\mathcal O_Y(Y)\to\mathcal O_X(X)$, which is $\varphi$ by the first step, is of finite presentation: $S$ is a finitely presented $R$-algebra.

source.place: Lemma Tag 02H6, proof, first paragraph: 'By Morphisms, Lemma 01TQ we see that R -> A is of finite presentation'

proof.text: *($\Rightarrow$) smoothness of $\varphi$.* Under the same assumption, $f$ is formally smooth [def-sbc-formally-smooth], so by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-formally-smooth-iff-ring-lifting] $\varphi$ has the square-zero lifting property: for every $R$-algebra $D$, ideal $N\subseteq D$ with $N^2=0$ and $R$-algebra map $S\to D/N$ there is a lift $S\to D$. Since $S$ is finitely presented over $R$ by the previous step, [lem-weil-pbc-fp-square-zero-lifting-smooth-ring-map] shows that $\varphi$ is smooth [def-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map]: $H_1(L_{S/R})=0$ and $\Omega_{S/R}$ is finite projective.

source.place: Lemma Tag 02H6, proof, first paragraph: 'By Lemma 02H4 we see that R -> A is formally smooth ... By Algebra, Proposition 00TN we see that R -> A is smooth' (Lemma 02H3 is not needed: U = X, V = Y)

proof.text: *($\Leftarrow$) local finite presentation.* Assume $\varphi$ is a smooth ring map [def-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map]; in particular $S$ is a finitely presented $R$-algebra. Then for every point $x\in X$ the affine open neighbourhood $U=X=\operatorname{Spec}S$ of $x$ and the affine open $V=Y=\operatorname{Spec}R$ satisfy $f(U)\subseteq V$, and the induced ring map is $\varphi$ (first step), which is of finite presentation; so $f$ is of finite presentation at $x$, hence locally of finite presentation, by the definition [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation].

source.place: Definition Tag 01TP (definition-finite-presentation), instance with U = Spec S, V = Spec R; cf. Lemma Tag 01TQ

proof.text: *($\Leftarrow$) formal smoothness.* By [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map-square-zero-lifting], a smooth ring map $\varphi$ has the square-zero lifting property: for every ring $D$ with a ring map $R\to D$, ideal $N$ with $N^2=0$ and $R$-algebra map $g:S\to D/N$ there is an $R$-algebra map $S\to D$ lifting $g$. By [lem-weil-pbc-affine-formally-smooth-iff-ring-lifting] $f=\operatorname{Spec}\varphi$ is formally smooth [def-sbc-formally-smooth]. With the previous step, $f$ is locally of finite presentation and formally smooth, i.e. smooth in the sense of [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms].
